title: A nontrivial centred valuation on a smooth curve and its etale coordinate
statement: Let $K$ be a field and $C$ a smooth integral finite-type $K$-scheme of dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Identify the function field $k(C)$, the local ring at the generic point, with $L$ [def-sc-function-field]. Let $A\subsetneq L$ be a valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring] containing $K$ and suppose $\operatorname{Spec}A\to C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] induces this field identification at the generic point. The image $c$ of its closed point is a closed point of $C$, and $A=\mathcal O_{C,c}$ as subrings of $L$; this is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. There exist an affine neighbourhood $U$ of $c$ and an etale $K$-morphism $u:U\to\mathbf A^1_K$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space]. If $x\in A$ is its coordinate, $y=u(c)$ and $F=K(x)$, then $x$ is transcendental over $K$, $L/F$ is finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], $A\cap F=\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1_K,y}$, and $A$ is a localization at a prime ideal of an etale algebra over $A\cap F$. The induced residue-field extension $\kappa(c)/\kappa(y)$ is finite separable. If $K$ is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed], this residue-field extension is the identity under the given embeddings.

source.place: Tag 054L (lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space), dimension-one case; varieties.tex Tag 0B8Y (lemma-regular-point-on-curve) for the DVR; Temkin proof of Theorem 2.1.8, printed pp. 12--13, with an etale coordinate instead of its arbitrary-uniformizer assertion.

proof.text: Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $C$, and let $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to C$ be the given morphism. Its stalk map at the closed point is a local homomorphism $R=\mathcal O_{C,c}\to A$. All these rings map into $L$: on an affine open containing $c$, the germ embedding into the generic stalk identifies the fraction field with $L$, and the stalk is its localization at the prime representing $c$. Compatibility of stalk maps with generization and the prescribed identity on the generic field show that $R\to A\to L$ is this canonical inclusion. Thus $R\subseteq A$ and $\mathfrak m_A\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$. If $c=\eta$, this inclusion would be $L\subseteq A$, contradicting $A\subsetneq L$. Hence $c\ne\eta$.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves, affine stalks; local maps and generization compatibility

proof.text: The point $c$ is closed. Otherwise choose a proper specialization $z$ of $c$. The chain $\overline{\{z\}}\subsetneq\overline{\{c\}}\subsetneq C$ of irreducible closed subsets would have length two, contradicting $\dim C=1$. Strictness on the right follows from $c\ne\eta$, and strictness on the left from the $T_0$ property of schemes. Choose a finite-type affine chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}D$ containing $c$ from the finite-type hypothesis. The prime $\mathfrak q$ representing $c$ is maximal and nonzero: the zero prime represents $\eta$. The stalk identification gives $R=D_{\mathfrak q}$, a local domain with fraction field $L$. Its prime chains have length at most one, since the corresponding chains of irreducible closed subsets of $V$, and their closures in $C$, have length at most one. The chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak qD_{\mathfrak q}$ has length one. Thus $\dim R=1$.

source.place: Tag 0B8Y, lemma-regular-point-on-curve, opening local-dimension reduction; prime-chain argument written out without separatedness

proof.text: A field is Noetherian, so $C$, of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}K$, is Noetherian; in particular its stalk $R$ is Noetherian. Smoothness over the field implies that every local ring of $C$ is normal, by the geometrically-normal theorem applied with the identity field extension. Therefore $R$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian normal local domain, and the normal-local-domain DVR criterion makes $R$ a discrete valuation ring. This applies over an arbitrary, possibly imperfect, field.

source.place: Tag 056T, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal; algebra.tex Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr (5) implies (1)

proof.text: Choose a generator $t\ne0$ of $\mathfrak m_R$. Since $R\to A$ is local, $t$ belongs to $\mathfrak m_A$. For $z\in L^\times$, write $z=a/b$ with nonzero $a,b\in R$. By the unit-times-uniformizer theorem write $a=ut^r$, $b=vt^s$ with $u,v\in R^\times$ and $r,s\ge0$. If $r\ge s$, then $z=(u/v)t^{r-s}\in R$. If $r<s$ and $z\in A$, put $h=s-r\ge1$. Then $t^{-1}=(v/u)t^{h-1}z\in A$, contradicting $t\in\mathfrak m_A$. Every nonzero element of $A$ is consequently in $R$, and $0\in R$; together with $R\subseteq A$ this proves $A=R$ inside $L$.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, final assertion; elementary fraction calculation using its unit-power form

proof.text: The smooth local normal form supplies an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $c$ and an etale $K$-morphism $u:U\to\mathbf A^d_K$ for some $d\ge0$. Here $U$ is nonempty and integral. The projection of affine $d$-space is smooth of relative dimension $d$, and an etale map is smooth of relative dimension zero. Composition therefore makes $U\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ smooth of relative dimension $d$, so $\dim U=d$. Moreover the etale ring map $K[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\to B$ is finitely presented, hence $B$ is finite type over $K$. Let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ represent the closed point $c$. The finite-type-domain dimension theorem gives $\dim B=\dim B_{\mathfrak q}=\dim R=1$. Thus $d=1$, giving the required coordinate $x=u^*(T)\in B\subseteq A$.

source.place: Tag 054L, lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space; relative dimension via Tag 02NL; algebra.tex Tag 00OS

proof.text: Put $P=K[T]$ and let $\varphi:P\to B$ send $T$ to $x$. Etaleness includes flatness, and the affine flatness criterion makes $B$ flat as a $P$-module. Since $P$ is a domain, flatness implies torsion-freeness. For $0\ne f\in P$, multiplication by $f$ on the nonzero ring $B$ is injective, so $\varphi(f)\ne0$ (otherwise it annihilates $1$). Hence $\varphi$ is injective, and the embedding $B\hookrightarrow L$ shows that $x$ is transcendental over $K$. Identify $\operatorname{Frac}P$ with $F=K(x)$. Apply the etale-algebra residue-field theorem at $(0)\subset B$, whose contraction in $P$ is $(0)$. The residue fields at these primes are respectively $L=\operatorname{Frac}B$ and $F$. It follows that $L/F$ is finite separable, with exactly the embeddings just specified.

source.place: Tag 01U5, lemma-flat-characterize; Tag 02GL, lemma-etale-over-field, applied at the generic point

proof.text: Let $y=u(c)$, and let $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\subset P$. The closed-point affine dimension data give that $\kappa(c)/K$ is finite. The image $\alpha$ of $x$ in $\kappa(c)$ is algebraic over $K$, and $P/\mathfrak p=K[\alpha]$ is a field (a finite-dimensional domain over $K$). Thus $\mathfrak p$ is a nonzero maximal ideal, $y$ is closed, and $\kappa(y)=K[\alpha]$ is finite over $K$. Set $R_0=P_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1_K,y}\subset F$. The polynomial regularity theorem makes $R_0$ regular local, while the finite-type-domain dimension theorem and $\dim K[T]=1$ give $\dim R_0=1$. The regular-local DVR criterion makes $R_0$ a DVR, in particular a valuation ring of $F$.

The stalk map of $u$ at $c$ identifies $R_0\to R=A$ with the inclusion induced by $P\to B\to L$. It is local, so $A$ dominates $R_0$. Apply the valuation-intersection theorem to the valuation ring $R_0$ of $F$, the extension $F\hookrightarrow L$, and the dominating valuation ring $A$. It gives $A\cap F=R_0=\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^1_K,y}$ as subrings of $L$.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves; local stalk map and the existing dominating-valuation intersection theorem

proof.text: Base change $P\to B$ along $P\to R_0$. The algebra $B_0=R_0\otimes_PB=(P\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}B$ is etale over $R_0$. Since $\varphi(P\setminus\mathfrak p)$ avoids $\mathfrak q$, this localization has the prime $\mathfrak q_0=(P\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}\mathfrak q$. Its localization is $B_{\mathfrak q}$: both rings invert exactly all the elements of $B\setminus\mathfrak q$, and the inverse maps send a fraction to the same fraction. The affine-stalk theorem identifies $B_{\mathfrak q}$ with $R=A$ by the germ map. Consequently $A=(B_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}$, a localization at a prime of an etale algebra over $R_0=A\cap F$. The ring meaning of etale here agrees with the scheme meaning by the affine etale comparison.

source.place: Tag 00U2, lemma-etale, base change; schemes.tex Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves; iterated localization by its fractions

proof.text: Apply the etale-algebra residue-field theorem a second time, now to $P\to B$ and $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$. It says that the actual map $\kappa(y)\to\kappa(c)$ is finite separable. If $K$ is separably closed, the already proved finite extension $\kappa(y)/K$ is algebraic, and the separably-closed algebraic-extension theorem makes $\kappa(y)$ separably closed. By the definition of separable closedness its finite separable extension $\kappa(c)$ is trivial. Hence the displayed residue map is an isomorphism, or the identity after identifying the two fields through the given embeddings. This does not assert that either residue field is $K$ when $K$ is imperfect.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NV-9f969b020 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: NV lem-trf-curve-centred-valuation-dvr 9f969b02, stage 1, one commit with the item and the report. No new nodes and no repairs needed. Statement: the same as the unsplit base (clones/live) except for two added definition references, def-sc-function-field and def-sbc-affine-space; nothing is weakened. Each step was read against its cited statements. (1) The local stalk map plus functoriality under generization give R=O_{C,c}⊆A, and c≠η because A⊊L. (2) c is closed by a length-two chain argument, and dim R=1 follows from a chart D_q; no separatedness is used. (3) Normality comes from smoothness over any field (056T with the identity extension), then the Noetherian dim-1 normal criterion gives a DVR; the 0B8Y perfect/separable clause is correctly avoided. (4) A=R by the unit·t^n fraction argument; I checked the t^{-1} contradiction. (5) The 054L normal form gives some d; relative-dimension permanence and dimension over a field give d=dim U, and 00OS with q maximal gives d=1. Stacks 054L itself only gives some d. (6) Flatness gives torsion-freeness, so K[T]→B is injective and x is transcendental; the étale residue node at (0) gives L/K(x) finite separable. (7) κ(c)/K is finite (closed-point node), so p is maximal and nonzero; P_p is regular of dimension 1, hence a DVR. (8) Domination plus the Nagata intersection node give A∩F=R_0. (9) R_0⊗_P B=S^{-1}B is étale (00U2), and localizing at S^{-1}q gives B_q=A. (10) The residue node at (q,p) gives κ(c)/κ(y) finite separable; κ(y) is separably closed when K is, so the extension is trivial, with no claim that κ(c)=K. Edge cases checked: K[T]_(T); a nonlinear closed point over a non-closed field; imperfect separably closed K at the point (T^p−a), where κ(c)≠K but κ(c)/κ(y) is trivial; a doubled-origin line. No cycle (341-node closure). The DAG search found no node already stating this item. The 21 declared generic tool_uses are accepted. Review in review.md.
